models.title: After-tax FVIF under accrual taxation
models.summary: Per-unit accumulation when returns are taxed annually at a uniform rate.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Accrual Taxes, printed p. 256 (PDF p. 266), Equation 2; Kozlowska case [1 + 0.07(1−0.20)]^20 → EUR297,357 on EUR100,000
relationship.translation_notes: Variable exponent T on a dimensionless base (allowed). Decimal rates; T is a dimensionless year count. Distinct from plain FVIF by the embedded annual tax drag (overlap note in integration). Dimensional check: dimensionless base to a count power = dimensionless factor.

variables.definition: Pretax annual return, in decimal form
variables.context: same investment, uniform annual tax regime and horizon as fvif

variables.definition: Uniform annual tax rate on investment income, in decimal form
variables.context: same investment and horizon as R

variables.definition: Investment horizon in years (dimensionless count)
variables.context: same investment and tax regime as R

variables.definition: After-tax accumulation factor per unit of currency invested
variables.context: same investment, tax regime and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Single uniform tax rate on the full return; after-tax proceeds reinvested at the same pretax return R (per source).
limitations: Compounds the tax drag: the gain share consumed exceeds the nominal rate over long horizons (per source Exhibit 25).
No inflation adjustment (see inflation-adjusted sibling); no realization timing within the horizon.

sources.evidence: Page states the identical after-tax FVIF equation with a worked example applying it.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.method: Source: [1 + 0.07×0.80]^20 = 1.056^20 = 2.9735696, reported as factor 2.97357 (EUR297,357). Tolerance covers rounding.
references.provenance: Published result: LM4 Kozlowska case, printed p. 257 (PDF p. 267)

references.method: Source Q4 variant: [1 + 0.04×0.80]^20 = 1.032^20 = 1.8775609, reported as factor 1.87756 (EUR187,756). Tolerance covers rounding.
references.provenance: Published result: LM4 purchasing-power case, printed p. 264 (PDF p. 274)

rejection_cases.reason: A 100% annual tax rate is outside the modeling domain (guard tx < 1).

models.inverse_notes: R = (fvif**(1/T) − 1)/(1 − tx) requires T ≠ 0 and tx ≠ 1; tx = 1 − (fvif**(1/T) − 1)/R requires R ≠ 0, T ≠ 0. T = 0 gives fvif = 1 (no time, no accumulation). Substitution check: fvif=2.97357, tx=0.2, T=20 recovers R=0.07 within rounding. Algebraic only.

gaps: Quantity meanings pre_tax_return, accrual_tax_rate, year_count, after_tax_fvif are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.

Overlap note: nearest existing ID is engineering-finance--lump-sum-future-value-discrete; this record is genuinely distinct by embedding the uniform annual tax drag in the compounding rate (PDF Eq2 vs plain FVIF).
No existing catalog record duplicates this relationship; catalog-inventory checked 2026-11-04.

models.summary: Per-unit accumulation when gains are taxed once at liquidation.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Deferral of Taxes, printed p. 258 (PDF p. 268), Equation 3; Kozlowska deferral case factor 3.2958 → EUR329,576
relationship.translation_notes: The +tCG term returns the tax on the untaxed cost of the initial unit (per source). Variable exponent on dimensionless base. Decimal rates. Dimensional check: dimensionless throughout.

variables.context: same investment, deferred-gains regime and horizon as fvif

variables.definition: Investment horizon in years (same meaning as accrual sibling)
variables.context: same investment and tax regime as R

variables.definition: Capital-gains tax rate applied once at liquidation, in decimal form
variables.context: same investment and horizon as R

variables.definition: After-tax accumulation factor per unit invested under gains deferral

assumptions: Full pretax compounding with a single liquidation tax on the gain; cost basis equals the initial unit (B = 1; see basis sibling for B < 1).

Single rate and horizon; graduated holding-period rates need extension.
